evidence.title: AI-based automatic patient positioning in a digital-BGO PET/CT scanner: efficacy and impact
evidence.outcome: Excessive patient off-centering before and after correction of the camera calibration
evidence.effect: Off-centering > 2.5 cm decreased from 49% (143/292, p < 0.001) before recalibration to 27% (38/140) afterward; the manual-positioning comparator remained virtually unchanged across the recalibration date.
evidence.quote: Also, after recalibration, 27% (38/140) of the studies had off-centerings > 2.5 cm for dBGO, which was significantly better than the 49% (143/292, p < 0.001) before recalibration or the 54% (185/343, p < 0.001) for dLYSO (Fig. 5 B).

evidence.title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
evidence.venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance following iterative error feedback, corrective updates, and repeat validation
evidence.effect: Across iterative testing, monitoring, and updates, AUC increased by 10.8% (from 0.83 to 0.92) and accuracy by 16.9% (from 0.77 to 0.90). Individual update effects could not be isolated.
evidence.quote: Over this time, AUC increased by 10.8% (from 0.83 to 0.92), accuracy by 16.9% (from 0.77 to 0.90), sensitivity by 4.8% (from 0.84 to 0.88), and specificity by 30.0% (from 0.70 to 0.91).

evidence.title: Closed-Loop Quality Assurance for Production Clinical AI Documentation
evidence.outcome: Physician complaint resolution and regressions during closed-loop quality improvement
evidence.effect: Across thirteen US hospital sites, the closed-loop system resolved physician complaints with zero regressions on 42 tracked cases across 1,089 optimization iterations.
evidence.quote: A closed-loop quality system deployed across thirteen US hospital sites resolved physician complaints with zero regressions on 42 tracked cases across 1,089 optimization iterations, while a deterministic assembly-agent replacement cut H+P trace latency from 19.6 s to 10.8 s (−8.8 s, 95% CI [−10.5, −7.1] s;  n = 100 pre,  n = 100 post).

evidence.title: Optimizing efficiency of a custom clinical decision support tool improves adult congenital heart disease care
evidence.venue: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
evidence.outcome: False positive alerts per month after case review and corrective PDSA changes
evidence.effect: False positive alerts fell from median 35 (IQR 12) to 15 (IQR 7) per month; department code introduced new false positives (7 per month).
evidence.quote: With the implementation of PDSA, the number of false positive alerts dropped from 35 (12) alerts per month to 15 (7) (median (IQR)).

evidence.title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
evidence.outcome: Technical defects and clinical assessment following monitoring-driven corrective updates
evidence.effect: Following iterative testing, monitoring, feedback, and updates, average technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%; clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0 in an uncontrolled before–after comparison.
evidence.quote: The average proportion of technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%, while the clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0.

evidence.title: Sisyphus' Alert: The Uphill Struggle to Improve Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Alert dismissal without further action after iterative corrective modifications
evidence.effect: Modifications did not significantly decrease dismissal without further action (88%).
evidence.quote: Modifications also did not cause a significant decrease in how frequently the alert was dismissed without further action being taken (88%).

evidence.title: Real-world use and evaluation of a generative AI chatbot for Parkinson's disease information: a prospective observational study
evidence.outcome: Emergency-response activation following incident remediation and re-testing
evidence.effect: The previously missed suicidality conversation activated the intended protocol on re-test after revision; concurrent configuration changes limit attribution, and verification applies only to this specific failure.
evidence.quote: After the post-window protocol revision, the conversation in which the emergency response had not been triggered was re-tested and now activates the intended protocol; because the current configuration differs from the evaluated one in further respects ( Supplementary Appendix Table S1 ), this verifies remediation of the specific failure only.

evidence.title: Real-World Evaluation of Large Language Models in Healthcare (RWE-LLM): A New Realm of AI Safety & Validation
evidence.outcome: Correct medical advice across iterations incorporating error identification and system enhancement
evidence.effect: Correct medical advice improved from ∼80.0% (pre-Polaris) to 96.79% (Polaris 1.0), 98.75% (Polaris 2.0), and 99.38% (Polaris 3.0), without a concurrent comparator.
evidence.quote: Performance metrics demonstrated substantial safety improvements between iterations, with correct medical advice rates improving from ∼80.0% (pre-Polaris), to 96.79% (Polaris 1.0), to 98.75% (Polaris 2.0) and 99.38% (Polaris 3.0).

evidence.title: Ensuring fair, safe, and interpretable artificial intelligence-based prediction tools in a real-world oncological setting
evidence.outcome: Resolution of identified data-feed failures and recovery of data-health metrics
evidence.effect: EHR data-feed outages during the weeks of May 16th and May 23rd, 2022 were investigated and resolved; data-health metrics returned to expected ranges.
evidence.quote: Using the data health monitors in place and collaboration between the data teams at both institutions, the issues were quickly resolved, which is reflected in our data health metrics returning to their expected ranges.

commentary.bottom_line: Eight of nine studies of corrective-action cycles after AI errors report fewer errors or better performance, but most lack a comparison group and none isolates the effect of root-cause analysis itself. Consistent endorsement by frameworks and regulators supports adopting the practice, while the size of its benefit remains uncertain.

perspectives.view: Two studies had comparators. In PET/CT, off-centering over 2.5 cm fell from 49% to 27% after recalibration, while the manual comparator stayed flat. In mammography, AUC rose from 0.83 to 0.92, though the study could not isolate single updates. The other seven are uncontrolled or offline, and one found no change, so certainty is low.

Corrective changes can introduce new failures. In one study, false positive alerts fell from a median of 35 to 15 per month, yet a department code added 7 new ones per month. A German chatbot study confirmed on re-test that one missed suicidality conversation now triggered the protocol, but this check covered only that failure.

In one mammography program, technical defects fell from 9.0% to 1.0% over repeated cycles of testing, feedback, and updates. In the null study, alert dismissal without further action stayed at 88% after iterative modifications, which suggests that model fixes may not change clinician response. One offline report found that investigating data-feed outages returned data-health metrics to expected ranges.

A closed-loop system across thirteen US hospital sites resolved 42 physician complaints with zero regressions, but it required 1,089 optimization iterations, which implies sustained engineering effort. Correct advice in the Polaris calls rose from about 80.0% to 99.38% over three versions, measured offline without a comparator. No study reported the staffing or cost of root-cause review.

Only the German chatbot study included limited English proficiency users and older adults, and it was descriptive and verified a single fix. No study reported Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations. It is therefore unknown whether corrective cycles catch failures that occur more often in those groups.

Eleven sources endorse the practice. FDA draft guidance for AI-enabled devices expects corrective and preventive action that draws on complaints and other quality data. Utah HB 452 requires mental health chatbot operators to document actions taken to mitigate harmful interactions. CHAI, FUTURE-AI, and NIST frameworks rest on expert consensus rather than trial evidence.

commentary.research_gap: No study compared sites that performed structured root-cause analysis with sites that did not, and none separated the effect of the investigation from concurrent model or configuration updates. Controlled or stepped-wedge designs could close this gap if they measured recurrence of the original failure, new failures introduced by fixes, staff time, and outcomes in Medicaid and limited English proficiency populations.
commentary.underserved_note: One descriptive study from Germany included limited English proficiency users and older adults, and no test included Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving those groups cannot yet assume that corrective cycles will prevent recurring failures in their patients.
